title: Shortfall action tiles — staffing & pricing protocol
body:
Purpose: Distill a compact, executable playbook (action tiles) finance + HR + product can run when a 6–12 week runway stress is detected due to token volume collapse, delayed renewals, or unexpected model infra spend. This is a working playbook intended for rapid ops decisions - not the final governance doc.

Summary in one line:
If run-rate falls by >=18% vs baseline forecast for two consecutive weeks OR monthly infra spend variance > 20% vs forecast, stand up the Shortfall Response and execute tile sequence below.

Triggers (primary):
- Token volume drop: two-week trailing decline >= 18% vs forecasted baseline.
- Revenue: one material cancellation > $250k ARR or cumulative churn > 10% of expected MRR in 30 days.
- Cost shock: monthly infra spend > 120% of budgeted (unexpected GPU spot/region surcharge).
- Combined minor signals: three out of five product routes show >15% latency-driven cost escalation.

Activation timeline (fast lane):
T0: Finance declares Shortfall Response. Slack channel: #shortfall-response. Stand-up within 24 hours.
T+24h: Emergency leadership huddle (CFO, Head of People, Head of Eng, Head of Product, Head of Sales). Decide Tier (A/B/C).
T+72h: Execute Tier actions (see tiles). Progress updates every 48 hours until stabilized.

Tiering rationale (quick):
- Tier A: structural shortfall (runway erosion >= 10% of remaining runway in 3 months). Requires hiring pause + targeted pricing actions.
- Tier B: transient shock (single-month overspend or revenue blip) — prefer non-headcount mitigations first.
- Tier C: exploratory signal — monitoring + soft gating (no immediate freezes)

Action tiles (ordered, combinable):
1) Hiring quick-freeze (tile HQF):
   - Scope: pauses all external offers not yet accepted and defers internal role approvals for 14 days. Exceptions: critical SRE/production oncall roles documented and approved by COO.
   - Expected immediate saving: 0.7–1.1% monthly burn per 10 offers paused (assumes average ramp comp + benefits).
   - Owner: Head of People (Aisha Patel point).

2) Contractor rebase & convert (tile CRC):
   - Reduce contractor budgets by reprioritizing to emergency tickets; convert high-impact contractors to 60% hours with 30-day notice.
   - Savings estimate: $120k–$420k over 90 days depending on contractor mix.
   - Owner: Eng leads + People ops.

3) Feature throttles & tiering (tile FTT):
   - Product to identify high-token routes (top 10 by token volume) and apply temporary quota/tiering for non-enterprise customers; enable caching aggressively.
   - Short-term revenue impact: up to 2–4% churn risk vs substantial cost reduction on high-variance routes.
   - Owner: Head of Product + Solutions Eng.

4) Price-floor & micro-surcharges (tile PFMS):
   - Institute a minimal token price floor on new customers / re-pricing for heavy routes, and add micro-surcharge for very high peak bursts. Communicate as temporary resilience surcharge.
   - Legal/comms template: finance to draft FAQ and support scripts within 48 hours.
   - Owner: Finance (lead) + Go-to-market alignment.

5) Dedicated capacity / slab reassign (tile DCSR):
   - Reassign committed GPU pools to the highest margin workloads; temporarily pause low-margin slab autoscale.
   - Operational impact: requires 72–120h ops window to shift capacity safely.
   - Savings: immediate token-cost reduction of 8–18% on affected scopes.

6) Deferred capital & non-payroll spend (tile DCN):
   - Delay planned marketing campaigns, travel, physical office spend, and vendor renewals that aren’t mission-critical.
   - Owner: Finance + functional owners.

7) Targeted voluntary separation package (tile VSP):
   - If Tier A persists past 30 days, design a VSP focusing on senior ICs who opt-in; ensure minimal product continuity.
   - Owner: People + Finance; governance required.

8) Emergency revenue acceleration (tile ERA):
   - Sales/CS to run 30-day closure sprints on top 15 expansion opportunities; prioritize deals that bring committed reserved/dedicated revenue or multi-month prepay.
   - Owner: Head of Sales + CS.

Headcount impact model (example baseline -> Tier A compressed):
- Baseline headcount (company-wide): 150 FTE
- Freeze + contractor conversion (after 90 days): net headcount delta -7 FTE equivalent (5 contractors -> reduced hours)
- If VSP run: potential opt-in 8–14 FTEs over 60 days.
- Rough payroll saving band (run-rate): $700k–$1.8M annualized depending on seniority mix.

Quick scenario micro-forecast (90-day look):
- Baseline: monthly burn $2.1M, runway 9 months on current cash.
- Downside scenario (18% token volume drop + 1 large churn): monthly burn + cost shock -> $2.4M (worse), runway 7.8 months.
- Execute tiles HQF + CRC + FTT + DCN -> expected immediate burn reduction to $2.05M and runway recalibrates to ~9.2 months (after wind-down adjustments).

Risks & mitigations: 
- Morale risk from hiring freezes: mitigate with transparent Q&A, time-boxed commitments, and clear exceptions process.
- Customer backlash from throttles/surcharges: pre-empt via customer success outreach and temporary credits for impacted enterprise accounts.
- Engineering velocity drop: preserve critical hires (SRE, infra) and maintain a minimal hiring sign-off workflow with COO.

Governance & decisioning checklist (first 72h):
- Finance: confirm data signal (two-week trailing vs forecast), produce one-page delta scenario with runway impact.
- People: freeze execution list + exceptions table.
- Product: top 10 token routes and recommended throttle plan.
- Ops/Infra: quick slab/dedicated capacity map and estimated reassign time.
- Sales/CS: list of convertible pipeline and top-10 at-risk customers.
- Communications: draft customer-facing FAQ and internal all-hands note.

Template escalation matrix: 
- Week 1: Emergency huddle -> HQF/CRC/FTT (soft launches)
- Week 2: Review impact -> PFMS/DCN if Tier A persists
- Week 3–4: Re-evaluate metrics; consider VSP/ERA as last-resort or acceleration measures

Post-mortem & rewind plan:
- Weekly cadence during response; after 60 days, compile a post-mortem documenting which tiles triggered, estimated savings, customer impact, and a recovery runway plan to re-open hiring and reverse surcharges.

Appendix — quick math assumptions used in the playbook: 
- Average fully-burdened hire cost (annual): $220k; monthly ≈ $18.3k.
- Average contractor monthly charge (FTE eq): $12k.
- High-token route cost multiplier: 1.6x baseline per-token spend when unthrottled.
- Latency-driven cost spike probability on unoptimized routes: 12–22% per month during high-peak weeks.

Open questions / flags to resolve:
- Does Legal require pre-approval for temporary surcharges in EMEA? (action: Legal q by T+24h).
- Are there pre-existing supplier SLAs that block immediate slab reassignments? (Ops to verify).
- Do any active offers include signing bonuses that would materially change the HQF savings? (People to audit active offer stack).

Next steps (immediate owner actions):
- Finance (Aisha): produce one-slide delta with runway impact and confirm activation criteria met. Due: T+6h.
- People (Daniel): publish freeze list + exceptions workflow and notify recruiters. Due: T+12h.
- Product (Marisol): identify top-10 token routes, recommended throttles, and customer impact note. Due: T+24h.
- Ops (Ethan): capacity map with 72h reassign estimate. Due: T+36h.

Notes: keep this doc lightweight — operational teams should copy into their runbooks and attach evidence at linked artifacts. This will be the canonical quick-response playbook until the formal Shortfall SOP lands in Confluence.

(End of draft)
